cards.text: The fight against Midian is on, and Gideon is right in the middle of it. Then the men of Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes, march up to him. And friend, they did NOT come to say congratulations.

cards.question: What has the men of Ephraim so upset with Gideon?

answers.text: He didn't call them to fight Midian
He kept the plunder for himself
He put Manasseh in charge of them

cards.question: The men of Ephraim bring their complaint to Gideon calmly and quietly.

cards.text: Gideon could fire right back at them. Instead he says, “Now what have I accomplished compared to you?”

cards.question: Gideon tells Ephraim their leftover grapes beat the whole grape harvest of Abiezer, his own clan. What is Gideon saying?

answers.text: Ephraim did more than he did

cards.text: Then he reminds them that God delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into THEIR hand. He asks what he was able to do compared to them.

cards.question: Once Gideon gives the men of Ephraim the credit, their anger against him ___.

cards.text: One kind answer, and the whole fight is over. That's getting chewed out for leaving somebody off the group chat and saying, “Leave YOU out? Friend, you ARE the group chat.”
Now Gideon and his three hundred men cross the Jordan, exhausted but STILL chasing. They come to the town of Succoth.

cards.question: Gideon asks the men of Succoth for ___ because his troops are ___.

cards.text: He tells them he's still chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian. Two KINGS, friend, and his guys are running on fumes.

cards.question: The leaders of Succoth are happy to feed Gideon's tired men.

cards.text: Not even close. They ask, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?”

cards.question: Gideon answers Succoth with a warning for when the LORD hands him the two kings. What does he say he'll do to them?

answers.text: Tear their flesh with thorns and briers
Burn their whole city to the ground
Take away all their flocks and herds

cards.text: From there Gideon goes up to Penuel and asks them for the same thing. Same tired men, same polite ask, new town.

cards.question: The men of Penuel give Gideon the ___ response as the men of Succoth.
Gideon has a warning for Penuel too. What does he say he'll tear down when he returns in triumph?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian, are in Karkor with about fifteen thousand men. That's all that's left of the armies of the people of the east.

cards.question: Only about fifteen thousand men are left. How many swordsmen from the armies of the east have already fallen?

cards.text: So Gideon goes up by the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah. Fifteen thousand men are out there, and the exhausted guy is the one doing the CHASING.

cards.question: Gideon's attack on the army at Karkor takes them by surprise.
When Zebah and Zalmunna flee, what happens to the two kings of Midian?

cards.text: And their entire army is routed. Two kings with a whole army behind them, and now the only men behind them are Gideon's.
On his way back along the Ascent of Heres, Gideon captures a young man from Succoth and questions him.

cards.question: The young man writes down for Gideon the names of Succoth's seventy-seven ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then Gideon walks into Succoth and says, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me,” and he repeats their own words right back to them. That's the “remember what you said?” text, except he brought two KINGS as the receipts.

cards.question: Gideon warned Succoth back when they refused him bread. Now what does he do to the elders of the city?

answers.text: Disciplines them with thorns and briers
Forgives them and goes on his way
Makes them carry all his supplies

cards.question: Gideon leaves the tower of Penuel standing.

cards.text: He pulls down the tower of Penuel and kills the men of the city. Next, Gideon asks Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?”

cards.question: How do Zebah and Zalmunna describe the men they killed at Tabor?
Gideon tells the kings that the men killed at Tabor were his ___.

cards.text: Then Gideon tells them, “As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”

cards.question: When Gideon tells Jether, his firstborn son, to kill the kings, Jether draws his sword.

cards.text: Jether doesn't move. He's fearful, because he's still a youth.

cards.question: Zebah and Zalmunna tell Gideon to get up and kill them himself. What reason do they give?

answers.text: As the man is so is his strength
As the sword is so is the blow
As the king is so is the land

cards.text: So Gideon kills Zebah and Zalmunna himself and takes the crescent ornaments from the necks of their camels. That's where we stop for now, friend, but trust me, Gideon's story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "Leave YOU out? Friend, you ARE the group chat.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 quotes "remember what you said?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Card 4 quotes Gideon saying "Now what have I accomplished compared to you?" That line gives away the answer to card 5, which asks what Gideon means about the gleanings of Ephraim. The right answer is "Ephraim did more than he did." Card 4 should set up the exchange without stating the meaning card 5 tests.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card adds nothing new from the passage. "One kind answer, and the whole fight is over" repeats card 7's answer that the anger subsides, and the rest is a group chat joke. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward, such as card 6.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Card 9 says the men are "exhausted but STILL chasing." The very next card asks the baker to fill the blank "his troops are ___" with "exhausted." Card 9 should tell the crossing without using that word, or card 10 should blank something else.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "So Gideon goes up by the caravan route" uses "So," which makes the attack a result of the kings being at Karkor with fifteen thousand men. Judges 8:11 only says "And Gideon went up." The text doesn't connect the two.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "He repeats their own words right back to them" says Gideon's quote matches what Succoth said. It isn't an exact match. In 8:6 Succoth said "give bread to your army." In 8:15 Gideon quotes them as saying "give bread to your weary men."

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.

findings.problem: "Jether doesn't move" goes beyond Judges 8:20, which says "the young man did not draw his sword." The card should say what the text says.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The answers are three sayings of the same shape: "As the man is so is his strength," "As the sword is so is the blow" and "As the king is so is the land." The baker can only pick the right one by guessing the exact wording of the kings' saying. Nothing earlier lets them reason it out. The card should ask what the kings mean instead, such as that killing them takes a grown man's strength.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question reads "What has the men of Ephraim so upset with Gideon?" The subject "the men" is plural, so it should say "have."
findings.question: The docs have no rule about grammar in card text. Should the checker report grammar errors like this, and under which rule?
